name: Fleshhook
overview: The fleshhook was an essential utensil used in the tabernacle service and priestly duties, specifically for handling meat during sacrifices. Scripture describes fleshhooks as made primarily of brass, highlighting their durable and sacred use in the altar's operations (Exodus 27:3; 38:3). Additionally, 1 Samuel 2:13-14 illustrates their practical role in the priests' ministry, where a three-toothed fleshhook was used to retrieve meat from cooking vessels, emphasizing the careful and reverent handling of sacrificial offerings.
